title: Coherent log ideals and their unsaturated and saturated chart gluings
statement:
Let $(Y,N)$ be a locally Noetherian fs log scheme and $\mathcal H\subset N$ a nonempty coherent log ideal [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Its algebraized ideal $K=\alpha(\mathcal H)\mathcal O_Y$ is a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent], and on every strict etale chart $\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ with fine saturated monoid chart $P\to A$ and $\mathcal H$ generated by a finite nonempty set $E\subset P$, its pullback is $(\alpha(e):e\in E)\subset A$. Use additive notation for $P$, and put $Q_e=\langle P,h-e\ (h\in E)\rangle\subset P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ and $Q_e^{\mathrm{sat}}=\{q\in P^{\mathrm{gp}}:nq\in Q_e\text{ for some }n>0\}$. Both $Q_e$ and $Q_e^{\mathrm{sat}}$ are finitely generated integral monoids with group completion $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$. For a monoid $T$, $\mathbf Z[T]$ denotes the ring of finite sums of symbols $z^t$ with $z^tz^{t'}=z^{t+t'}$. The fine log schemes with charts
$$\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q_e])$$
glue on their common localizations, and descend along strict etale covers, to a fine log scheme $Y_0\to Y$ universal for making $\mathcal H$ locally principal among fine log schemes. Replacing every $Q_e$ by $Q_e^{\mathrm{sat}}$ gives compatible charts that glue and descend to an fs log scheme $Y_s\to Y$ with the corresponding universal property among fs log schemes. There is a canonical morphism $s:Y_s\to Y_0$; it is finite on underlying schemes (preimages of affine opens are spectra of finite algebras). These constructions commute with strict etale restriction. Tensor products are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Here a fine log scheme has etale-local charts by finitely generated integral monoids, without a saturation requirement; a log morphism is strict when its source log structure is the one associated to the inverse image of the target log structure and its structure map.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-log-ideal-algebraization-descent] to $(Y,N,\mathcal H)$; an fs log structure is fine. It gives exactly $K=\alpha(\mathcal H)\mathcal O_Y$, its finite-type quasi-coherence, and the formula on every stipulated strict etale chart.

source.place: VIII 3.3.7 and 3.4.2, printed pp. 107 and 110; finite image ideal via the algebraization input.

proof.text: On each such chart apply [lem-trf-log-ideal-affine-atlas-gluing]. This gives the asserted monoids and group completions, both tensor-chart gluings $U_0,U_s$, their overlaps, principal pulled-back ideals and strict base-change compatibility. Apply [lem-trf-log-ideal-chart-lifting-criterion] to fine, respectively fs, test objects. Its covering and overlap clauses give compatible local lifts. The source-local morphism clause of [lem-trf-polarized-fine-log-etale-descent], which requires no polarization, glues them uniquely, proving both local universal properties.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17--3.1.21 and 3.3.5--3.3.9, printed pp. 101 and 107--108; affine atlas and local lifting inputs, then source-local morphism descent.

proof.text: The strict base-change clause of [lem-trf-log-ideal-affine-atlas-gluing] preserves the fixed-chart construction on restrictions. Two local constructions on the same log base admit unique maps to one another by the universal properties of Step 2; the composites are identities by uniqueness. The comparisons respect further strict etale restriction and satisfy the triple cocycle by uniqueness. This compares different charts and generating sets on overlaps by restriction.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8, printed pp. 107--108; strict restriction and uniqueness comparisons.

proof.text: In either local construction the generator loci are exactly its affine $e$-charts by [lem-trf-log-ideal-saturation-chart-finiteness]. Apply [lem-trf-principal-log-ideal-tautological-polarization] to its pulled-back ideal and the sections $E$. The resulting relatively ample line bundles are intrinsic to the ideals, so the comparisons of Step 3 preserve them with their cocycles. Apply [lem-trf-polarized-fine-log-etale-descent] to obtain $Y_0,Y_s$ as fine, respectively fs, log schemes. Pulling any test object back to this cover and descending its unique local lifts proves the global universal properties; conversely a lift pulls back the principal ideal. Uniqueness gives strict etale compatibility.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.9, printed pp. 107--108; generator-torsor polarization and effective polarized descent.

proof.text: The fine universal property gives the unique $s:Y_s\to Y_0$. Locally it is the comparison of [lem-trf-log-ideal-saturation-chart-finiteness], since the explicit chart map and $s$ are both lifts over $Y$. That lemma identifies its chart preimages and proves local finiteness. The strict etale chart pullbacks cover $Y_0$; their open affine $e$-charts therefore form an etale cover of $Y_0$, hence an fpqc cover by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-finite] to obtain global finiteness in the asserted affine sense. Chart formulas and restriction compatibility follow from the same lemma and uniqueness.

I checked this against that node's current statement: the clause holds for fine T and Z over a fine S, which here means a fine or fs test object, U_0/U_s and the fs chart U. (2) Overlap identity: Q_e ∋ f−e, so Q_e+N(e−f)=Q_f+N(f−e), and saturation commutes with it. Lifting: a lift is a monoid map Q_e→M_T, unique by cancellation, and it extends to Q_e^s because fs stalks are saturated. Covering clause: m=g(e)+b and g(e)=m+a give a+b=0. (3) Comparisons follow from the atlas base-change clause plus uniqueness, so elementary is correct. (4) The generator loci are the affine e-charts. The polarization node gives L, with transitions α(h_f−h_e), X_{s_h} = generator locus (α^{-1}O^×=M^×), ampleness in the sense of 01PS with n=1, and relative ampleness because V_e×_A A' is affine. These are exactly the hypotheses of polarized descent, which yields Y_0 fine and Y_s fs. (5) s^{-1}(X_e^0)=X_e^s and the 1⊗z^f span, so the base changes are finite. The e-charts are a small-étale covering of Y_0, hence fpqc by fpqc-finer-than-etale, and fpqc-descend-finite applies.
